title: The symmetric monoidal structure on $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ and $C$ be as in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf]; for instance $C$ is the
small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ of a scheme ([def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]) or the
category of profinite sets with the coherent topology, and $\mathcal A=\Ab$ with
$\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and unit $\mathbf Z$, or $\mathcal A=\Mod_R$ for a commutative ring $R$.
For sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ define:

- the *tensor product* $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G:=a(\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)$, with
  $a$ sheafification ([def-weil-pbc-sheafification]), and on morphisms $a(\varphi\otimes_p\psi)$;
- the *unit* $\mathbf 1_{\Sh}:=a(\underline{\mathbf 1})$;
- the *associator*
  $(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G)\otimes\mathcal H\cong\mathcal F\otimes(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal H)$
  as the composite
  $$
  a\bigl(a(\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)\otimes_p\mathcal H\bigr)\cong a\bigl((\mathcal F\otimes_p\mathcal G)\otimes_p\mathcal H\bigr)\xrightarrow{a(\alpha)}a\bigl(\mathcal F\otimes_p(\mathcal G\otimes_p\mathcal H)\bigr)\cong a\bigl(\mathcal F\otimes_pa(\mathcal G\otimes_p\mathcal H)\bigr),
  $$
  where $\alpha$ is the objectwise associator and the outer isomorphisms are $a$ applied to the
  maps $\eta\otimes_p\mathcal H$, $\mathcal F\otimes_p\eta$ (units of $a$), which are invertible
  after $a$ by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso];
- the *unitors* and the *symmetry* in the same way from the objectwise ones and the unit maps
  $\underline{\mathbf 1}\to a(\underline{\mathbf 1})$.

Then $(\Sh(C,\mathcal A),\otimes,\mathbf 1_{\Sh})$ is a symmetric monoidal category, and
sheafification $a\colon(\mathrm{PSh}(C,\mathcal A),\otimes_p)\to(\Sh(C,\mathcal A),\otimes)$ is
strong symmetric monoidal, with structure isomorphisms
$a(F)\otimes a(G)=a(aF\otimes_paG)\cong a(F\otimes_pG)$ and
$\mathbf 1_{\Sh}=a(\underline{\mathbf 1})$. For $\mathcal A=\Ab$, $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G$ is the
sheafified objectwise $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and the unit is the constant sheaf
$\underline{\mathbf Z}$ ([def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]).

proof.text: Write $i$ for the full inclusion of sheaves into presheaves, and $\eta_P:P\to iaP$ for the unit of sheafification. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] says that precomposition with $\eta_P$ bijects maps to every sheaf. Thus $\eta_P\in W$ by the Hom criterion in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso]. For a sheaf $S$, extend $\mathrm{id}_{iS}$ across $\eta_{iS}$ to obtain $\epsilon_S:aiS\to S$. Then $i\epsilon_S\eta_{iS}=\mathrm{id}$; uniqueness of extension applied again gives $\eta_{iS}i\epsilon_S=\mathrm{id}$. These identifications are natural by the same uniqueness. We will use the unit naturality equation $i(a f)\eta_P=\eta_Q f$ for $f:P\to Q$.

The presheaf tensor, its unit $I$, and its objectwise structure isomorphisms are those of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf]. Functoriality of $a$ and of this tensor gives the stated bifunctor on sheaves and unit $aI$. Here is a precise comparison for every finite tensor expression, keeping its brackets and all occurrences of $I$. Choose presheaves $P_j$, sheaves $S_j$ and maps $q_j:P_j\to iS_j$ in $W$. Evaluate an expression $B$ in presheaves as $P_B$, and evaluate it in sheaves as $S_B$ using the bifunctor just defined. At a variable use $q_j$; at $I$ use $q_I=\eta_I$; at a binary expression $B=(D E)$ set
$$q_B=\eta_{iS_D\otimes_p iS_E}\circ(q_D\otimes_p q_E):P_D\otimes_pP_E\longrightarrow i\,a(iS_D\otimes_p iS_E).$$
Induction on the expression proves $q_B\in W$: it holds at variables by assumption and at $I$ by step 1; clause 2 of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] gives it for $q_D\otimes_pq_E$, and composition preserves $W$ since $a$ is a functor. In particular $a(q_B)$ is invertible. This argument includes an expression consisting only of the unit; it does not assume a nonempty family of variables.

Define the associator by the composite in the statement, using the inverse of $a(\eta_{iF\otimes_p iG}\otimes_p iH)$ on its left and $a(iF\otimes_p\eta_{iG\otimes_p iH})$ on its right. Both maps are invertible by clause 1 of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] and step 1. Explicitly define the left unitor as
$$\epsilon_F\circ a(\lambda^p_{iF})\circ a(\eta_I\otimes_p iF)^{-1}:a(iaI\otimes_p iF)\longrightarrow F,$$
and the right unitor by $\epsilon_F\circ a(\rho^p_{iF})\circ a(iF\otimes_p\eta_I)^{-1}$. Define symmetry as $a(\beta^p_{iF,iG})$. These are natural isomorphisms: functoriality gives naturality before taking inverses, and naturality of an invertible family also gives naturality of its inverse.

source.place: Second paragraph: definitions and naturality of the four structure maps

proof.text:
For the comparisons $q_B$ of step 2, [lem-sfb-sheaf-tensor-unit-comparison] gives, for each basic associator, unitor or symmetry $t^p:P_B\to P_{B'}$ and its sheaf version $t^{\mathrm{Sh}}:S_B\to S_{B'}$,
$$i(t^{\mathrm{Sh}})q_B=q_{B'}t^p.\tag{*}$$
Indeed $q_{(DE)}=d(q_D,q_E)$ in that lemma's notation, the unit comparison is $\eta_I$, and its four formulas are precisely (*) for these four maps. Its arbitrary $f,g,h$ may be taken to be the comparisons of compound subexpressions, so this application does not assume that a sheafification unit is an isomorphism of presheaves.

source.place: Second paragraph: basic structure-map comparison, for arbitrary leaf maps

proof.text:
We check coherence rather than assume that unspecified canonical maps cancel. Equation (*) propagates to structure maps inside any tensor expression. Indeed, if $if\,q_D=q_{D'}f_p$ and $ig\,q_E=q_{E'}g_p$, then bifunctoriality and unit naturality give
$$i\bigl(a(if\otimes_p ig)\bigr)q_{(D E)}
=\eta_{iS_{D'}\otimes_p iS_{E'}}\bigl((if\,q_D)\otimes_p(ig\,q_E)\bigr)
=q_{(D'E')}(f_p\otimes_p g_p).$$
This proves the propagation by induction on the surrounding expression; composition propagates (*) by substitution, and for an inverse structure map it follows from
$$i(t^{\mathrm{Sh}})q_B=q_{B'}t^p\quad\Longrightarrow\quad i((t^{\mathrm{Sh}})^{-1})q_{B'}=q_B(t^p)^{-1}.$$
Only the structure isomorphisms are inverted; $q_B$ need not be an isomorphism of presheaves. For coherence specialize to $P_j=iS_j$ and $q_j=\mathrm{id}_{iS_j}$ in step 2. For the two paths $u,v:S_B\to S_{B'}$ around a pentagon, triangle or either hexagon, we therefore obtain $iu\,q_B=q_{B'}u_p$ and $iv\,q_B=q_{B'}v_p$. The objectwise monoidal identities in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf] give $u_p=v_p$. Since $q_B\in W$, the Hom criterion of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso], applied to the sheaf $S_{B'}$, makes precomposition with $q_B$ injective. Hence $u=v$. For involutivity, (*) for the two symmetries gives $i(\beta_{G,F}\beta_{F,G})q_{(FG)}=q_{(FG)}\beta^p_{iG,iF}\beta^p_{iF,iG}=q_{(FG)}=i(\mathrm{id})q_{(FG)}$; injectivity of this precomposition gives $\beta_{G,F}\beta_{F,G}=\mathrm{id}$. Thus the defined tensor and maps give a symmetric monoidal category. No general coherence or localization theorem is invoked.

For sheafification itself use step 2 with $S_j=aP_j$ and $q_j=\eta_{P_j}$. The unique extension of $q_B$ to a map $c_B:aP_B\to S_B$ is $\epsilon_{S_B}\circ a(q_B)$, and is invertible by step 2. At a variable this map is the identity. At a unit it is also the identity; at a binary expression in two variables it is
$$c_{F,G}=a(\eta_F\otimes_p\eta_G):a(F\otimes_pG)\xrightarrow{\sim}a(iaF\otimes_piaG)=aF\otimes aG,$$
by unit naturality and $\epsilon_{aQ}a(\eta_Q)=\mathrm{id}$, the latter following from the uniqueness of extension across $\eta_Q$. Clause 3 of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] also states this invertibility directly. The tensorator in the question is $c_{F,G}^{-1}$ and the unit comparison is the identity of $aI$. Naturality of these comparisons follows from unit naturality.

source.place: Third paragraph: invertibility and naturality of the sheafification comparisons

proof.text:
To identify the comparisons for compound expressions, first note that $i(c_D)\eta_{P_D}=q_D$ and $i(c_E)\eta_{P_E}=q_E$. Hence
$$i\bigl((c_D\otimes c_E)c_{P_D,P_E}\bigr)\eta_{P_D\otimes_pP_E}
=\eta_{iS_D\otimes_piS_E}(q_D\otimes_pq_E)=q_{(DE)},$$
by bifunctoriality and unit naturality. Uniqueness of extension therefore gives the recursion
$$c_{(DE)}=(c_D\otimes c_E)c_{P_D,P_E}.$$
Equation (*) was proved in step 4 for arbitrary leaf comparisons and extends inside contexts by step 5. For a basic presheaf structure map $t^p:P_B\to P_{B'}$, it yields
$$i(t^{\mathrm{Sh}}c_B)\eta_{P_B}=q_{B'}t^p=i(c_{B'}a(t^p))\eta_{P_B}.$$
Uniqueness of extension gives $t^{\mathrm{Sh}}c_B=c_{B'}a(t^p)$. Substituting the recursion for $c_B,c_{B'}$ gives the four equations
$$\alpha^{\mathrm{Sh}}(c_{F,G}\otimes\mathrm{id})c_{F\otimes_pG,H}
=(\mathrm{id}\otimes c_{G,H})c_{F,G\otimes_pH}a(\alpha^p),$$
$$\lambda^{\mathrm{Sh}}_{aF}c_{I,F}=a(\lambda^p_F),\qquad
\rho^{\mathrm{Sh}}_{aF}c_{F,I}=a(\rho^p_F),\qquad
\beta^{\mathrm{Sh}}_{aF,aG}c_{F,G}=c_{G,F}a(\beta^p_{F,G}).$$
These are precisely the associativity, unit and symmetry compatibilities of a strong symmetric monoidal functor (written in the direction $c$). Thus $a$ has the asserted structure, with the specified inverse tensorator.

source.place: Third paragraph: recursion and four monoidal-functor compatibility equations

proof.text: For $\mathcal A=\Ab$, clause 1 of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-presheaf] evaluates the presheaf tensor as $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal G(U)$ and its unit as the constant presheaf $\mathbf Z$. The definitions above therefore give its sheafification as the tensor of sheaves. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $a(\underline{\mathbf Z})$ is exactly the constant sheaf with value $\mathbf Z$. This identifies the tensor and unit, without replacing the additive tensor by the cartesian product.
